finding.claim: SQL injection in /search: the q parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL query. An unauthenticated attacker can use UNION SELECT to read any table in shop.db, such as users or credentials, and can break out of the LIKE clause.
finding.sink: db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") at app.py:12

trace.note: @app.route('/search') with no auth decorator or middleware
term taken directly from the query string, no validation
term interpolated into the SQL string, not bound as a parameter
query results returned via jsonify, so UNION-based data exfiltration is directly visible in the response

finding.guards_checked: No authentication, input validation, escaping or allowlist on the route. No before_request hooks or middleware exist in the file. The query is not parameterized. The other two routes (/product, /by-owner) do use bound parameters, so they are not affected.

verdict.reason: app.py:11-12 takes request.args q and interpolates it into an f-string SQL query with no auth, validation or parameter binding, and app.py:13 returns the rows via jsonify, so UNION-based exfiltration is visible to an anonymous caller.
